edges.effect_quant: A 2022 meta-analysis of 8 randomized trials involving 472 patients found no significant overall improvement in IBS symptom severity or responder rates, despite individual trials reporting benefit.
edges.population: adults with moderate-to-severe irritable bowel syndrome
edges.mechanism: FMT can clearly alter gut microbial composition in IBS, but symptom benefit appears inconsistent because IBS is multifactorial and recipient biology may determine whether donor strains meaningfully change function rather than simply colonization patterns. This makes it more plausible as a subgroup-responsive intervention than as a broadly effective IBS therapy.
edges.summary: FMT changes the microbiome in IBS, but symptom relief is inconsistent across trials. Some randomized studies report meaningful improvement in IBS severity scores, whereas pooled trial evidence and newer mechanistic follow-up work suggest that microbiome shifts often occur without a reliable parallel improvement in global symptoms.
edges.caveats: Differences in donor selection, administration route, bowel prep, and IBS subtype likely contribute to the conflicting results. At the moment this is not a settled beneficial edge; it is better interpreted as a mixed and formulation-sensitive intervention with uncertain generalizability.
